name: AnalysisWorkbench
intent: Stage-path query builder over an ontology object set or a governed dataset — source, filter, traverse, derive — with a route badge, a spec summary and a diagnosis for every empty result.
when: Building an ad-hoc analysis a user will save and re-run
Any staged query the user assembles rather than types
whenNot: Rendering a finished result -> use Chart or DataTable
Filtering an existing table -> use Filter

chooseOver.component: A form of dropdowns over a query API
chooseOver.because: The workbench names WHY a result is empty — source-empty, no-time-column, filters-excluded-all, all-unlinked — instead of showing a blank chart, and carries the lineage of the spec that produced it.

session.note: The spec, its result and the saved set; the host owns persistence.

renderSourceConfig.note: Source stage body — one of exactly two stages whose options differ per mode.

renderTraverseConfig.note: Traverse / Join stage body — the other one.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Saved analyses are keyed by id; object sets by the ontology's own identity.

renderTraverseConfig.description: Traverse or Join stage body, per mode

states.default: A source stage awaiting a set.
states.built: A stage path with a route badge and a spec summary.
states.empty: A named diagnosis rather than a blank result.
states.saved: The spec is referenced by id so a tile re-runs it under the viewer's own permissions.

forbiddenPlacement: a dashboard tile — bind the tile to a SAVED analysis by reference instead
evaluationCriteria: An empty result always states which diagnosis applies.
The spec, not the result, is what gets saved.
Exactly two stages are supplied by the host — the two whose options differ per mode.

lineage.authoredBy: Promoted from the WC3 analysis perspective (2026-08-26)
notes: The spec/run/diagnose seam around it was already pure and exported; only the surface was stuck.
Promoted in group B of the missing-widgets template review.
